key_insight: CA-WCP adds class-aware, asymmetric conformal bounds for 3D segmentation volumes, aiming to keep uncertainty calibrated under distribution shift.
clinical_relevance: This could make volumetric tumor and organ segmentations more trustworthy by flagging when predictions are uncertain and by reducing overconfident errors in clinical workflows.
method: Uses latent-space density-ratio weighting to adjust for covariate shift.
Learns separate lower/upper volume quantiles for asymmetric error control.
Scales bounds with class-specific factors from validation false-positive and false-negative rates.
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2020 and a synthetic multi-organ CT shift benchmark, observed 95% Clopper–Pearson coverage included the nominal 90% level for every class, with 8–14% narrower intervals than symmetric weighted conformal prediction.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate validation estimates of class-specific error asymmetry and shift weighting, so calibration may be sensitive to dataset mismatch or unstable density-ratio estimation.
paper_title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
